notice: Educational screening summaries. Not diagnoses. Published study results are labeled as such and are not OcuScan performance. Sources do not imply clinical endorsement of OcuScan.

references.authors: Ueno Y, Oda M, et al.
references.title: Deep learning model for extensive smartphone-based diagnosis and triage of cataracts and multiple corneal diseases
references.used_for: Anterior-segment research framework; corneal and lens module context
references.evidence_summary: Published study result — not OcuScan performance: model trained on slit-lamp images distinguished 36 cataract/corneal diseases in 9 categories (AUC 0.968–0.998); smartphone images used for the testing dataset only.

references.authors: Taki Y, Ueno Y, Oda M, et al.
references.title: Analysis of the performance of the CorneAI for iOS in the classification of corneal diseases and cataracts based on journal photographs
references.used_for: Anterior-segment research framework; on-device classification context
references.evidence_summary: Published study result — not OcuScan performance: smartphone app classified journal anterior-segment photographs with top-1 positive predictive value 0.75 and top-3 above 0.80.

references.authors: Maehara H, Ueno Y, Yamaguchi T, et al.
references.title: Artificial intelligence support improves diagnosis accuracy in anterior segment eye diseases
references.used_for: Anterior-segment research framework; clinician-assistance context
references.evidence_summary: Published study result — not OcuScan performance: AI support significantly increased clinician accuracy for several anterior-segment categories; smartphone misclassification examples documented.

references.authors: Bastawrous A, Rono HK, Livingstone IAT, et al.
references.title: Development and Validation of a Smartphone-Based Visual Acuity Test (Peek Acuity) for Clinical Practice and Community-Based Fieldwork
references.used_for: Distance visual-acuity test design (tumbling-E, randomization, repeatability expectations)
references.evidence_summary: Published study result — not OcuScan performance: Peek Acuity agreed with ETDRS within 0.07 logMAR with test-retest variability ±0.029 logMAR in Kenyan field settings.

references.authors: Steren BJ, Young B, Chow J
references.title: Visual acuity testing for telehealth using mobile applications
references.used_for: Home/telehealth acuity testing context and calibration warnings
references.evidence_summary: Published study result — not OcuScan performance: home mobile-app acuity tests compared against in-office measurements; supports telehealth use with validation caveats.

references.authors: Perera C, Chakrabarti R, Islam FMA, Crowston J
references.title: The Eye Phone Study: reliability and accuracy of assessing Snellen visual acuity using smartphone technology
references.used_for: Smartphone acuity reliability context; app-quality variation warning
references.evidence_summary: Published study result — not OcuScan performance: smartphone Snellen assessment evaluated for reliability and accuracy against standard charts.

references.authors: Tofigh S, Shortridge E, Elkeeb A, Godley BF
references.title: Effectiveness of a smartphone application for testing near visual acuity
references.used_for: Near-vision screening design
references.evidence_summary: Published study result — not OcuScan performance: smartphone near-acuity app evaluated for effectiveness.

references.title: Mobile app Aston contrast sensitivity test
references.used_for: Contrast ladder design; repeatability expectations across devices
references.evidence_summary: Published study result — not OcuScan performance: mobile contrast apps repeatable (near 0.26–0.37 log units) but recorded higher sensitivity than printed tests; device display matters.

references.title: The reliability of the Pelli-Robson contrast sensitivity chart

references.evidence_summary: Published study result — not OcuScan performance: smartphone color test agreed with Ishihara in controls (bias −0.01) but wider limits in pathology (bias −0.50); authors call for further testing.

references.title: Comparison of a Smartphone Application with Ishihara Pseudoisochromatic Plate for Testing Colour Vision
references.used_for: Color test display-dependence limitation; same-modality repeat recommendation
references.evidence_summary: Published study result — not OcuScan performance: app plates differ from Ishihara plates; screen size, resolution, brightness, and saturation affect results; use one modality consistently.

references.evidence_summary: Published study result — not OcuScan performance: RGB smartphone pupillometry agreed with a commercial device when the pupil was found, but detection failed in nearly a quarter of scans.

entries.name: Facial movement asymmetry
entries.observable_finding: Observable left/right difference in facial movement amplitude during guided expressions (eyebrow raise, eye closure, smile, cheek puff).
entries.description: Observable left/right difference in facial movement amplitude during guided expressions (eyebrow raise, eye closure, smile, cheek puff).
entries.screening_method: Guided-expression capture with landmark tracking; per-region amplitude comparison; repeatability across sessions.
possible_associations: Movement patterns sometimes confused with nerve conditions — the app cannot distinguish causes
cannot_conclude: Whether a neurological condition is present
limitations: Front camera cannot assess nerve function directly
Head rotation mimics asymmetry
Single-session result may vary
entries.action: Repeat the test facing the camera directly. Seek urgent care for sudden facial weakness, especially with speech changes, arm weakness, or vision changes. Otherwise consider professional evaluation if asymmetry is new or persistent.
entries.recommended_action: Repeat the test facing the camera directly. Seek urgent care for sudden facial weakness, especially with speech changes, arm weakness, or vision changes. Otherwise consider professional evaluation if asymmetry is new or persistent.
emergency_signs: Sudden facial droop with trouble speaking
Arm weakness or severe headache with facial weakness
emergency_flags: Sudden facial droop with trouble speaking
Arm weakness or severe headache with facial weakness

entries.name: Eyelid position asymmetry
entries.observable_finding: Relative difference in visible upper-eyelid opening between eyes estimated from landmarks.
entries.description: Relative difference in visible upper-eyelid opening between eyes estimated from landmarks.
entries.screening_method: Landmark-based eyelid-opening comparison in straight-ahead gaze.
limitations: Validation evidence for this landmark measurement is limited
Not a diagnosis of ptosis
Gaze angle and brow position affect measurement
Glasses and shadows reduce reliability
entries.action: Repeat with eyes looking straight ahead in even lighting. Consider professional evaluation if asymmetry is new, persistent, or affects vision.
entries.recommended_action: Repeat with eyes looking straight ahead in even lighting. Consider professional evaluation if asymmetry is new, persistent, or affects vision.
emergency_signs: Sudden double vision with drooping eyelid
Eyelid swelling with severe pain or fever
emergency_flags: Sudden double vision with drooping eyelid
Eyelid swelling with severe pain or fever

entries.name: Eye alignment difference
entries.observable_finding: Estimated difference in eye position or gaze-direction change during fixation and cover/uncover sequence.
entries.description: Estimated difference in eye position or gaze-direction change during fixation and cover/uncover sequence.
entries.screening_method: Fixation tracking with guided cover/uncover sequence; referral-oriented outcome.
limitations: Smartphone tracking is approximate
Cannot replace cover testing by a clinician
Head movement confounds results
entries.action: Repeat the guided cover test. Consider professional evaluation if misalignment is persistent or with double vision.
entries.recommended_action: Repeat the guided cover test. Consider professional evaluation if misalignment is persistent or with double vision.

entries.name: Pupil-size asymmetry
entries.observable_finding: Relative difference in visible pupil size between eyes, averaged over multiple frames.
entries.description: Relative difference in visible pupil size between eyes, averaged over multiple frames.
entries.screening_method: Multi-frame relative asymmetry index; invalid frames discarded with recorded reasons.
limitations: Millimeter diameters are NOT reported without physical calibration
Reflections and partial occlusion invalidate frames
Single frames are never used alone
RGB detection varies with eye color and lighting
entries.action: Repeat under stable, even lighting. Seek prompt evaluation if size difference is new, large, persistent, or with vision changes, headache, or drooping eyelid.
entries.recommended_action: Repeat under stable, even lighting. Seek prompt evaluation if size difference is new, large, persistent, or with vision changes, headache, or drooping eyelid.
emergency_signs: Sudden unequal pupils with vision change, severe headache, or injury
emergency_flags: Sudden unequal pupils with vision change, severe headache, or injury

entries.name: Pupil light-response pattern
entries.observable_finding: Relative temporal change in pupil appearance during a controlled safe light-exposure step. Flashlight steps are disabled unless exposure is reproducible and safe.
entries.description: Relative temporal change in pupil appearance during a controlled safe light-exposure step. Flashlight steps are disabled unless exposure is reproducible and safe.
entries.screening_method: Time-series response analysis; module self-disables without a safe reproducible stimulus.
required_hardware: Controlled safe light stimulus (not present in this build)
limitations: Phone flash is not a controlled clinical light source
Module disabled when safety or reproducibility cannot be assured
entries.action: If unavailable, treat as unable-to-assess. Do not attempt bright-light self-testing.
entries.recommended_action: If unavailable, treat as unable-to-assess. Do not attempt bright-light self-testing.
emergency_signs: Pupil changes with sudden vision loss or severe headache
emergency_flags: Pupil changes with sudden vision loss or severe headache

entries.name: Visible ocular-surface growth
entries.observable_finding: Visible fleshy or triangular region extending toward the cornea in the captured image.
entries.description: Visible fleshy or triangular region extending toward the cornea in the captured image.
entries.screening_method: Close-up surface imaging with conservative appearance thresholds; highlighted region shown to the user.
possible_associations: Growth-like appearance sometimes confused with pterygium or pinguecula — the app cannot distinguish
limitations: Experimental research module — not clinically validated
Cannot grade severity without validated labels
Image resolution limits surface detail
Cannot establish a diagnosis
entries.action: Review the highlighted region. Consider professional evaluation, especially with irritation, redness, or vision change.
entries.recommended_action: Review the highlighted region. Consider professional evaluation, especially with irritation, redness, or vision change.
emergency_signs: Severe eye pain or chemical exposure
emergency_flags: Severe eye pain or chemical exposure

entries.name: Ocular redness
entries.observable_finding: Increased redness of the visible scleral region and its distribution.
entries.description: Increased redness of the visible scleral region and its distribution.
entries.screening_method: Scleral-region color analysis in RGB/HSV/Lab under neutral lighting.
limitations: Validation evidence for phone-based redness grading is limited
Redness alone cannot identify a cause
Lighting and camera white balance affect color
entries.action: Avoid self-diagnosing the cause. Seek prompt care for pain, light sensitivity, vision change, discharge, injury, or chemical exposure.
entries.recommended_action: Avoid self-diagnosing the cause. Seek prompt care for pain, light sensitivity, vision change, discharge, injury, or chemical exposure.

entries.name: Scleral yellow discoloration
entries.observable_finding: Yellow discoloration of the visible sclera under lighting-controlled capture.
entries.description: Yellow discoloration of the visible sclera under lighting-controlled capture.
entries.screening_method: Calibrated scleral color comparison; failed calibration forces unable-to-assess.
limitations: Neonatal skin studies do not transfer to adult sclera
Requires neutral-white lighting calibration
Returns unable-to-assess when calibration fails
Cannot diagnose liver or blood conditions
entries.action: Repeat only under neutral lighting after calibration. Seek medical evaluation for persistent yellowing, especially with dark urine, pale stools, or abdominal symptoms.
entries.recommended_action: Repeat only under neutral lighting after calibration. Seek medical evaluation for persistent yellowing, especially with dark urine, pale stools, or abdominal symptoms.
emergency_signs: Yellowing with confusion, severe abdominal pain, or vomiting blood
emergency_flags: Yellowing with confusion, severe abdominal pain, or vomiting blood

entries.name: Visible corneal opacity
entries.observable_finding: Visible cloudy or opaque region on the corneal surface in the captured image.
entries.description: Visible cloudy or opaque region on the corneal surface in the captured image.
entries.screening_method: Conservative cloudiness cues on close-up corneal frames.
possible_associations: Cloudy appearance of undetermined cause — not a scar or infection diagnosis
cannot_conclude: Whether corneal disease is present or absent
limitations: OcuScan has no trained corneal-disease model; published models required slit-lamp training sets
Ordinary smartphone cameras have major limits for corneal detail
Conservative thresholds; normal result does not exclude disease
entries.action: Consider professional evaluation for any persistent opacity or with vision change, pain, or light sensitivity.
entries.recommended_action: Consider professional evaluation for any persistent opacity or with vision change, pain, or light sensitivity.

entries.name: Visible lens opacity
entries.observable_finding: Experimental screening for visible lens opacity appearance. Front camera is not equivalent to slit-lamp examination.
entries.description: Experimental screening for visible lens opacity appearance. Front camera is not equivalent to slit-lamp examination.
entries.screening_method: Appearance cues under supported capture method only.

limitations: Experimental research module — not clinically validated
Experimental module
Only reported when capture method supports it
Cannot determine whether a cataract is present

entries.recommended_action: Treat as screening only. Consider routine eye examination for vision changes.

Combined with symptom questionnaire only
